item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J03515","case1_error":"Reports one shortened component’s 5-inch length instead of the 15-inch length of three tied components.","case2_error":"Uses an invalid remaining-fence relation; its final expression equals 4000, not the reported 10000.","reason":"The first answers an intermediate quantity; the second constructs an erroneous relation and misreports its numerical value.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03516","case1_error":"Treats existing fuel as full capacity, then subtracts only the truck’s existing fuel to determine the refill amount.","case2_error":"Reports Yeon’s 1020 seeds instead of summing all three people’s seeds to obtain 1660.","reason":"The first uses erroneous refill relations; the second correctly calculates one person’s seeds but answers the wrong requested quantity.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03517","case1_error":"Uses salary minus necessities as taxes, ignoring the stated $18 remaining and incorrectly redefining expenses and leftovers.","case2_error":"Invents a repeating initial schedule, evaluates 10+3+10+1 as 14, and incorrectly treats the remainder as 14 hours.","reason":"The first omits a required budget component through erroneous relations; the second misrepresents the schedule and makes explicit arithmetic errors.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03518","case1_error":"Counts the other walker’s dogs as having two legs each, then rounds the resulting noninteger dog count.","case2_error":"Calculates a signed deficit of −14, but correctly concludes 14 hours are lacking; the answer marker conflicts with that conclusion.","reason":"The first has a clear modeling error. The second’s signed calculation and correct concluding magnitude leave an answer conflict rather than an unambiguous mathematical failure.","judgment":"uncertain"},{"pair_id":"J03519","case1_error":"Evaluates the correctly written calorie sum as 2175 instead of 1975.","case2_error":"Replaces the correctly calculated $5700 goal with money raised plus miscellaneous expenses, producing an incorrect remaining requirement.","reason":"The first is numerical evaluation of a correct expression; the second introduces an erroneous relation despite initially calculating the goal correctly.","judgment":"different"}]}
